title: Store JSON serialization change breaks immutable-install idempotency for same-id generations
wanted_capability: Byte-format-independent idempotency for content-addressed generation installs. install_immutable_json compares stored bytes against the new serialization; a deploy that changed store JSON from pretty-printed to compact made every previously installed generation dir refuse re-install of the SAME generation id (identical manifest_sha256, identical logical content) with StoreRequestError::InvalidInput. Because history_source_generation_id pins (producer, repo_history, namespace, repo_head, manifest_sha256), a repo whose HEAD does not move re-derives the same id forever, so finalize 422s on every attempt: this was the actual origin of the 5-day wampum git-history wedge (generation ghs_dffc1c8a installed 2026-08-19 pretty-printed, superseded by the coverage freeze; every later same-head upload refused at finalize). Fix direction: treat an existing generation dir whose manifest_sha256/descriptor match as idempotent success (semantic compare or re-derived hash compare), or pin the store serialization format as part of the on-disk contract. Remedy: deleted the superseded relic dir and the wedged upload; the next pass finalized fresh.
missing_primitive: semantic-equality (or descriptor-hash) idempotency check in install_immutable_json callers for generation artifacts
fallback_used: Deleted the pretty-JSON-era superseded generation dir and wedged upload record in the pod by hand.
evidence: crates/bbox-git-source/src/lib.rs:533-557 (generation id covers manifest_sha256, so same-head same-content re-derives the same id)
pod: ghs_dffc1c8a manifest.json pretty-printed (Aug 19, 242111 bytes) vs current upload compact (207729 bytes), identical entries
